_comment: Canonical set, keyed by cluster. decision: keep | merge | drop | defer. consumers: all (default) | none; none means held: the skill is in the catalog under .held/ and checked, but no consumer, link, bump PR, install or MCP response delivers it (DESIGN 3.2). publish: owner-approved marks a skill from a private repo or a local-only folder that the owner approved for publication; it is imported only after the M1 scrub. tools/inventory.py merges this into own-skills.{json,md}.

review-change.reason: One generic reviewer skill. Start from the research-mcp 1.1.0 text (SDD trace rules), strip project paths and refer to the project's AGENTS.md for the spec location and gates.
review-change.notes_on_diff: research-mcp is the kit template rendered for one project plus the 1.1.0 SDD adoption: LLD paths, @spec docstring rule, project scope rules and a changelog. The kit text is the generic base.

verify-change.reason: Same template/instance drift as review-change. Replace the {{FAST_GATE_CMD}} placeholder with 'the fast gate named in AGENTS.md' so one file serves every repo.
verify-change.notes_on_diff: Placeholder {{FAST_GATE_CMD}} vs tools/ci.sh --python-only; spec vs LLD wording; example claim and changelog added in research-mcp.

security-review.reason: Keep the seven generic checks; project-specific citations (LLD sections, ADR numbers) move to the project's AGENTS.md or a project overlay skill.
security-review.notes_on_diff: research-mcp adds LLD/ADR citations to each of the seven checks, Keychain specifics and a longer high-risk path list.

simplify-change.reason: Nearly identical; only the gate command and spec wording differ.
simplify-change.notes_on_diff: {{FAST_GATE_CMD}} vs tools/ci.sh --python-only; 'specification' vs 'LLDs'; version metadata and changelog.

run-project.reason: Project-specific by design (how to run this repo). Stays a kit template rendered into each project; not shared content.
